claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me begin with a few questions.

**First, how many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child – Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you, and I'm happy to help assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me start gathering the necessary details.

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in full-time education right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for clarifying that.

**Is Alex currently in work or receiving any income?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex has just started an apprenticeship actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's useful information. Thank you for letting me know.

**How much is Alex earning from the apprenticeship per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about the exact wage, but it's an apprenticeship here in England – you know, one of those proper training programs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Let me ask a slightly different way to help me assess this properly.

**Roughly, is Alex earning more or less than £120 per week from the apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of the exact amount to be honest. Is that important for the Child Benefit eligibility?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a fair question! Let me clarify by asking something more straightforward instead.

**Is Alex living with you in your household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Now, I have just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK? (This relates to your own eligibility to claim Child Benefit.)**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just to clarify a bit further for the assessment:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status under the UK immigration rules?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

I just need one final piece of information to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently receiving any other state benefits, or are you working? If you're working, are you earning above or below the High Income Child Benefit tax charge threshold (currently £50,000 per year for a single earner)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working, but I don't think I earn anywhere near £50,000 a year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me carefully review the rules based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex is not in full-time education
- Alex has started an apprenticeship
- Alex lives with you
- You are a British citizen
- Your income is below the High Income Child Benefit tax charge threshold

Based on UK Child Benefit rules, young people aged 16-19 can remain eligible if they are in approved education or training. An apprenticeship is considered approved training under the Child Benefit regulations, which means Alex can continue to qualify even though they are no longer in full-time education.

Since Alex is in an apprenticeship (approved training), lives with you, and you meet the residency and citizenship requirements with income below the threshold, Alex should be eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's a summary of why:

✓ **Alex's age and status**: At 17, Alex is within the eligible age range and is in an apprenticeship, which counts as approved training under Child Benefit rules.

✓ **Living arrangements**: Alex lives with you in your household.

✓ **Your eligibility**: You are a British citizen with income below the High Income Child Benefit tax charge threshold.

All the key requirements are met, so you should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already done so, you can make a claim through the official channels.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about this assessment?
